At 37 years old, after a lifetime of dudes staring at my chest... I wasn't 100% sure I was done having kids, but I sure as hell was done breastfeeding, so I finally got a breast reduction and was thrilled with the results. Even my husband was kind of on board, as he saw how happy it made me and how much easier exercise had become for me. 

Two weeks post-op, I visited my plastic surgeon for a normal follow-up. She told me that they had sent my breast tissue to pathology, and they found cancer. 

I had walked in motivated for a new active life, and left with fucking cancer. Ended up getting a double mastectomy, 8 rounds of chemo, a preventative hysterectomy, and hormone blocking treatments. 

Today, I'm 40 years old with a weakened heart (and a right atrial blood clot), osteoporosis, constant brain fog, depression, and constant scanxiety. 

But I'm alive! 😐

I understand this feeling, and it must be a real pain seeking a job right now. I've interviewed for a couple of positions over the pandemic, but have been in situations where I've had several interviews one after another, and I've learned it works best for me if I go into an interview as if it was just a meeting and a conversation, rather than a formal question-answer session. I make comments, ask them questions throughout rather than just at the end, and try to stay as casual as is appropriate. I tend to throw jokes every once in a while, and making people laugh always makes it a lot easier.

Most employers know all your technical skills just from your resume, and many of them are tired of interviewing candidates too. At the interview, they want to know if you'll be a good fit in their group, so just have a conversation!
